summary: Frontend E2E validation of MikiLab Pro iter 243 focused on 4 new features. FEATURE 4 (Corso shortcut da Piano) — PASS: entered as Direzione (gate 198505 -> onboarding-opt-panificio + confirm -> capo-gate-login -> admin@mikilab.de/Mikilab2026!), opened panel-piano-unico, iterated over piano-day-tab-* until finding a day with lots (piano-day-tab-lun had 1 batch). Clicked piano-batch-course-lun-0, piano-course-modal opened, piano-course-loading was visible briefly then 8 piano-course-phase-* elements rendered (Baguette a Lievito Madre course, cached). piano-course-close correctly dismissed the modal. FEATURE 2 (Corso a voce) — PASS: opened panel-ricette, searched 'Anima Integrale', clicked recipe-row-<id>, then course-recipe-<id>. recipe-course-panel appeared with course-speak-<id> initially reading 'Listen'/'Ascolta'. First click -> label toggled to 'Stop'/'Ferma'. Second click -> label reverted to 'Listen'/'Ascolta'. No console errors. FEATURE 1 (Importa il catalogo di Michele su nuova azienda) — BLOCKED (frontend gate bug, backend endpoint works): registered a new capo via auth-switch -> auth-name/email/password/confirm + auth-activation-code=198505 -> auth-submit. Registration succeeded (session created, top-right shows 'Test Capo'), but the new user is returned by /api/auth/me with role='user' instead of 'admin', so App.js line 482-498 keeps showing the 'CAPO ACCESS RESERVED' gate and NEVER renders master-console / panel-ricette. Result: import-catalog-btn is unreachable through the UI even though the /api/recipes/import-catalog endpoint itself is validated. REGRESSION — PASS: no blocking console errors (only benign 401 gate_required calls that happen before the gate cookie is set); piano weekly, day tabs and Capo Ricettario stay navigable through the full session.

critical.issue: New user created via activation-code path is stored with role='user' instead of role='admin'. Root cause: auth.py line 44 always calls _role_for_new_user() which only promotes the very first user in the whole DB. Owners of a NEW organization (activation-code branch) never become admin of their own org, so the Capo/Master UI is unreachable. Fix: promote to admin when the activation-code branch fired, e.g. "role": "admin" if _new_org_id != ORG_DEFAULT else await _role_for_new_user().

integration_issues.issue: Because new company owner has role='user' (see backend bug above), App.js gates the master-console behind the 'Sign in as Capo' screen even though the user is already authenticated (name visible in header). As a consequence data-testid='import-catalog-btn' is never rendered for the person who is supposed to use it, and Feature 1 cannot be completed via the UI.

action_items: Fix backend/auth.py auth_register: when the activation-code branch is taken (new organization), set role='admin' for the newly-created user so they can access their own Capo console. Suggested one-liner: 'role': 'admin' if _new_org_id != ORG_DEFAULT else await _role_for_new_user().
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py register (line 42-47): role assignment ignores the activation-code branch. Only the very first user in the whole DB is promoted to admin; every activation-code Capo is stuck as role='user'. This is a multi-tenant regression that fully blocks Feature 1 through the UI.

App.js line 482: master console visibility keyed only on user.role === 'admin'. Consider also unlocking when the user is the OWNER of their organization (e.g. user.is_owner or user.organization_id !== 'org_default' AND session matches). Currently a legitimate new Capo sees 'CAPO ACCESS RESERVED' even after a successful login.

RecipeList.jsx line 303: import-catalog-btn is inside the 'personal-empty-archive' block, which is only rendered inside the mikilab collection tab AND when list is empty. Since the new-capo can't reach the Ricettario at all (see above), the import feature is effectively dead-code from the UI perspective until the role bug is fixed.

rca of the issue: backend/auth.py auth_register never promotes activation-code users to admin; frontend App.js only shows master console (and therefore Ricettario + import-catalog-btn) when user.role === 'admin'. Combined effect: new Capo registered with the valid activation code is authenticated but cannot access any Capo functionality, defeating Feature 1 end-to-end even though the underlying /api/recipes/import-catalog endpoint is correct. Reproduction: fresh session -> gate 198505 -> capo-gate-login -> auth-switch to register -> fill name/email/password/confirm + activation 198505 -> submit -> /api/auth/me returns role='user'. Mitigation (1-line): auth.py line 44, replace 'role': await _role_for_new_user() with 'role': 'admin' if _new_org_id != ORG_DEFAULT else await _role_for_new_user().
